answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Only slash the bond when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task. As the horizon of trust expands, this mechanism ensures the integrity of decentralized systems, much like a cedar tree's resilience against disease. From a secure terrace, this bond-based system safeguards against malicious actors, fostering a more secure online environment.
